text:
Alex (Sales): FYI AcmeSec is asking if we can carve the POC out of their ISO scope. They want an "applicability statement" saying the PoC excludes long-term backups and analytics pipelines. quick take?
Maria (Security): Short answer: yes, for a limited POC we can provide an applicability statement, but we need a signed acceptance of the residual risks and clear boundaries (data types, retention, access).
Alex (Sales): They also want to know whether that changes pricing/contract for Dedicated vs Private POC. Priya, any commercial notes?
Priya (AE): Pricing-wise no automatic change — we price by capacity + add-ons. If they require extra controls (HSM/KMS integration, longer retention for audit), that can be a billable add-on. Otherwise standard POC pricing stands.
Emily (AcmeSec): To be explicit from our side: we need a short ISO alignment doc for the PoC covering scope, exclusions, and which documented ISMS policies will not apply during the PoC. Also an evidence list (cert copy, policy owners). Can you provide a template?
Maria (Security): I'll draft a concise applicability statement template. It will include:
- POC boundary (model endpoints, input types)
- Data handling limits (no PHI, masked data only)
- Excluded controls (long-term backups, cross-region replication, third-party analytics)
- Compensating controls (ephemeral keys, audit sampling)
- Risk acceptance clause signed by customer security
John (Solutions): From the tech side, we can run the POC in a Private VPC with minimal log retention and no cross-region replication. For evidence: we can provide config snippets and screenshots of KMS settings. Example config we usually send:
```
redwood.deploy:
  mode: private
  vpc: customer-vpc-id
  logging.retention_days: 7
  backups.enabled: false
```
Alex (Sales): Maria — can you include a short line about what we *cannot* exclude (eg: audit logs required for SLA/compliance inside the POC)? Emily, does that work?
Maria (Security): Yes — we can't exclude operational audit logs entirely. They can be minimized/rolled after X days but must be generated for incident traceability. I'll add a minimum retention (7 days) and explain why.
Emily (AcmeSec): 7 days is acceptable for the PoC. Also want to confirm: will Redwood redact tokens from logs? We need assurance on secrets handling.
John (Solutions): We can mask tokens and PII in logs by default. Will include a brief logging redaction note and example.
Priya (AE): Timeline: if Security signs the applicability statement this week, we can start POC infra in 3 business days. Any blockers on our side?
Alex (Sales): One more ask — customer wants a statement mapping PoC activities to ISO clauses (e.g., A.9 access control, A.12 ops). Maria, can you add that mapping (high level only)?
Maria (Security): Yes — I'll add a 1-page mapping table: which clauses are in-scope, which are out-of-scope for the PoC, and references to our policies (Access Control Policy, Encryption Standard, Retention Policy).
infra-bot: deploy request queued: poctest-acme-001. ETA infra build ~72h after "approved-by" tag.
Alex (Sales): Great. I'll send the draft applicability statement & PoC checklist to Emily and ask her to review/sign. Emily, can you confirm the signatory and their email?
Emily (AcmeSec): I'll be the signatory (emily@acme.example). Please send the draft and we'll review today. Thanks! :thumbsup:
Maria (Security): I'll post the draft in this thread in ~2 hours. It will be short (one page) and include the risk acceptance checkbox.
John (Solutions): I'll attach the sample config + a short runbook for the POC once Maria posts the doc.
Alex (Sales): Perfect — thanks everyone. Follow-ups: Maria posts draft, John posts runbook, Priya confirms pricing add-ons if requested.
